newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy would not need elections if Prodi fell - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Italy would not need elections if Prodi fell - Dini.

text.p: Italy would not have to hold new elections if the coalition government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi, which nearly fell apart last week, did actually collapse, Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Sunday.

He told reporters he doubted anyone was thinking seriously about new elections, adding: "Holding elections in 1997 would really mean excluding Italy from Europe and the single currency and that would be suicide."
Dini, who heads a small party in Prodi's centre-left coalition, said the government was working to meet a set of objectives laid out by the prime minister last week.

Prodi said he wanted to reinforce his majority and keep it united, press for constitutional reform and continue overhauling state accounts to ensure Italy was on the first train to the European single currency.

Dini told reporters on a visit here: "Only if this becomes impossible will we have to think of an alternative formula, securely based on the forces of the centre, on the parties which are part of the government coalition today."

Prodi's Olive Tree coalition ran into the worst crisis of its 11-month rule last week when a key ally, the hard-left Communist Refoundation, refused its parliamentary support for an Italian mission to nearby Albania.
Communist Refoundation's backing is crucial to the government in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), where the coalition lacks an outright majority.
